title: GCU vs Liberty: tuition, size, location
summary: Grand Canyon University (GCU) versus Liberty University (Liberty). Also searched as Liberty vs GCU. Scorecard table is sourced; prose is checked against those facts. UniRepository is not affiliated with either school.

sections.heading: How they differ
paragraphs: Liberty University and Grand Canyon University (Liberty vs GCU) are both private nonprofit institutions, as indicated by their ownership codes reported by College Scorecard. Liberty University is located in Lynchburg, while Grand Canyon University is based in Phoenix. In terms of undergraduate enrollment, Liberty has approximately 50,012 students, whereas Grand Canyon enrolls about 73,371 undergraduates. Tuition costs also differ, with Liberty charging $22,465 for in-state students compared to Grand Canyon's $17,850. These distinctions highlight key differences between Liberty University vs Grand Canyon University in size, location, and tuition.

sections.heading: Cost
paragraphs: When comparing Liberty University vs Grand Canyon University (Liberty vs GCU) in terms of cost, tuition fees are a significant factor. Additionally, the median debt for students who complete their programs differs between the two institutions. Graduates from Liberty University carry a median debt of $24,500, whereas those from Grand Canyon University have a slightly lower median debt of $22,114. These figures provide insight into the financial commitments associated with attending each university.
